column1: # patterns.tsv - the single source of truth for this skill's vendor patterns.
# scripts/scan.sh reads this file at runtime; `scan.sh --print-patterns` renders
# the equivalent `rg` one-liners for a script-less run. There is no second copy
# to keep in sync: adding a vendor is a one-line change here.
# Format: three TAB-separated columns, one group per line.
#   1 LABEL    group name, printed in the HIT SUMMARY and above the detail block
#   2 PATTERN  a ripgrep regex, applied with `rg -in` (case-insensitive, so never
#              write case variants; use \b word boundaries against prose noise)
#   3 NOTE     optional guidance printed with the group; use it for the judgment
#              a bare hit cannot carry (what to attribute it to, what NOT to flag)
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. A pattern must not contain
# a literal tab. Keep groups capability-shaped: one group per class of service,
# so the HIT SUMMARY stays readable and a new vendor usually joins an existing
# A group's absence is never evidence of a clean repo - see SKILL.md Step 3
# "do not read silence as cleanliness" and Step 2's residual judgment pass.

column1: Data, search, feature-flag and CMS SaaS
column3: check the Elasticsearch version pin (8.16+ has an AGPL option) and whether OpenSearch is the actual dependency
regionally critical for DPG deployments - M-Pesa/Daraja, Flutterwave, Paystack and Razorpay dominate outside the US/EU
read Laravel config/services.php and config/mail.php driver blocks as evidence; SMTP itself is an open protocol (R4) - the SaaS behind it is not
Twilio is not the only SMS vendor; Africa's Talking, MessageBird and Clickatell are the sole SMS path in several DPG codebases

column1: AI/ML hosted services (beyond the big-5 LLM vendors)
column3: hosted inference, ASR/TTS, GPU-on-demand and MLOps SaaS; downloading open weights from HuggingFace is NOT lock-in, hosted inference and gated tokens are
MapLibre, Leaflet, OpenLayers, osmdroid and OSM tiles are open - never flag them, and a repo with both a Mapbox and an osmdroid adapter is a GOOD sign (R2a)

column1: Web platform services (captcha, analytics tags, widgets)
column3: hardcoded tracking IDs in index.html count as evidence; mention any API token sitting beside the hit
a hosted RPC endpoint is swappable if the provider is injected; AWS QLDB is a fully proprietary ledger with no open equivalent
Oracle and SQL Server are proprietary servers reached through open-ish drivers - the server's license decides (R1)
ad networks and store SDKs are platform rails (R4): report them, and say plainly that an adapter contains but does not remove the coupling
a catalog alias or typed accessor is often the ONLY place a module names the vendor - count them to size the blast radius; a plugin on the classpath but never applied is declared-but-dark, not usage
proves a vendor is wired even when no manifest declares it (a Podfile with no Firebase entry while AppDelegate.m configures it); Bootstrap per R2 - use for coverage, not severity
EAS Build/Update/Submit and Expo push are proprietary services on an MIT SDK; app.config.js is executable and overrides app.json - never judge from app.json alone
